title: CUET 2026 Business Studies Mock Test 1
description: Memory-based CUET 2026 May 31 Shift 1 Business Studies question paper with solutions.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a function of management?

Match the levels of management in Column I with their primary responsibilities in Column II. Column I: (A) Top Management, (B) Middle Management, (C) Supervisory Management. Column II: (I) Supervising workers, (II) Implementing policies, (III) Formulating policies.
Which of the following is the first step in the planning process?

Given below are two statements: Assertion (A): Division of work increases efficiency and productivity. Reason (R): Specialisation enables workers to become experts in their assigned tasks. Choose the correct answer.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: Which of the following is an element of delegation?

Match the following financial markets with their characteristics. Column I: (A) Money Market, (B) Capital Market, (C) Equity Shares, (D) Debentures. Column II: (I) Long-term funds, (II) Treasury Bills, (III) Ownership capital, (IV) Borrowed capital.
Consumer Protection Act provides protection to consumers against:

Given below are two statements: Assertion (A): Leadership helps in influencing employees to achieve organisational goals. Reason (R): Leadership is an important element of directing. Choose the correct answer.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: Which of the following is a monetary incentive provided to employees?

Match the following marketing functions with their descriptions. Column I: (A) Product Planning, (B) Branding, (C) Promotion, (D) Packaging. Column II: (I) Informing customers about products, (II) Designing and developing products, (III) Creating a unique identity, (IV) Protecting and presenting products.
